chunks: And among what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from al-Nadr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
If a small animal falls into the well, or a person in janabah enters it, seven buckets are drawn from it. But if a bull dies in it, or wine is poured into it, then all of the water is drawn out.

So what these two reports contain regarding the obligation of drawing out all the water when a camel falls into it is what I act upon and according to which I give fatwa. That does not conflict with the first report in his saying, “a kurr of water,” when the questioner asked about the donkey and the camel, because it is not impossible that he عليه السلام answered with what specifically concerns the ruling of the donkey, and relied regarding the ruling of the camel upon what had already been heard from him concerning the obligation of drawing out all the water. As for wine, then all the water of the well is to be drawn out if any of it falls into it, in accordance with what the two reports contain, and that is also supported by...

key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janabah
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine, whose falling into the well necessitates drawing out all the water
key_terms.دَابَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ: a small animal whose falling into the well entails a lesser purification measure
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets, the specified amount to be drawn in certain cases
key_terms.كُرٌّ مِنْ مَاءٍ: a kurr of water, referenced in reconciling related reports
key_terms.نُزِحَ: water was drawn out from the well as a purification measure
key_terms.وُجُوبِ نَزْحِ ٱلْمَاءِ كُلِّهِ: the obligation of removing all the water from the well
key_terms.ٱلْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being evaluated for ritual purity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on well water if an animal falls into it or wine is poured into it?
ai.summary: This passage presents a legal ruling concerning the purification of well water after contamination by different causes. It distinguishes between cases requiring only a limited amount of water to be drawn and cases, such as death of a bull or the falling of wine, that require the entire well to be emptied, while also reconciling apparently differing reports.
